headline: THE CORE NESTING CLAIM IS REFUTED OUT OF SAMPLE. nested_pullback (HTF uptrend + LTF downtrend) is a genuine, distinct condition - 13-21% of bars, Jaccard 0.06-0.15 with pullback_to_support and 0.05-0.09 with fib_golden_pocket - and it beats its own control structure_trend@HTF in sample (Stouffer z=+1.87 over 14 cells) while failing out of sample (z=-0.54). Its OOS sign flips with the swing fractal width (+2.67 / -0.54 / +2.81 at k=2/3/5) and reverses per symbol between IS and OOS in all five contracts. All of its in-sample strength is in the 240/60 pair (z=+3.13), absent from 60/15 which has the identical 4:1 nesting ratio. No depth band works. The ONE survivor is nested_resumption - the pullback ENDING, algebraically nested_pullback AND break_of_structure@LTF - which is +0.118R on 157 OOS trades (win 48.4%, t=+1.22), positive out of sample in 4 of 5 symbols including both independent contracts, at all three swing widths and at doubled costs; removing either half of the conjunction destroys it despite 4-12x the sample. It is a hypothesis, not an edge: 0 of 224 OOS rows reach 20 trades and t=+1.22 is far below the free_t of 3.87. The incumbent nested_aligned is confirmed WORSE than no structure condition (z=-4.14 IS) and is bar-for-bar identical to mtf_aligned on any two-member frame.
caveats: Every arm INCLUDING the no-structure control is negative-expectancy in absolute terms (pooled -0.04 to -0.13 R). All comparisons are relative to a losing baseline; none of this is a discovered profitable system.

nested_resumption: 157 OOS trades in total for the pure arm, median 6 per (base, cell) row, 0 of 224 rows at n>=20. Its Stouffer z of +4.97 is a sign test on paired differences and is NOT evidence of a tradeable edge.
The 14 cells are not independent: MNQ/NQ/MES are one index complex and the three tf pairs on one symbol share bars. The independence-corrected figures use 240/60 only and three units.
NQ has no 15m file, so 60/15 covers 4 symbols.
One exit model throughout (ATRx1 stop, anchored 1.0/2.5 ATR targets, rth_only=False); every trade count and therefore every floor-dependent statement is conditional on that geometry.
Nothing here is live-eligible and nothing here has been through walk-forward selection - only a 60/40 split plus three disjoint slices.

nested_pullback_vs_no_structure.note: median Dexp NEGATIVE in both IS (-0.093R) and OOS (-0.049R)

nested_pullback_vs_htf_trend.note: htf_trend is the correct control because nested_pullback is a strict subset of it. The core claim does not survive OOS.

nested_resumption_vs_htf_trend.note: positive OOS and in 2 of 3 disjoint slices, but see the sample-size caveat

nested_aligned_vs_no_structure.note: the incumbent is measurably WORSE than no structure condition at all, reproducing the programme's earlier finding on independent construction

swing_parameter_sensitivity.method: Rebuilt every TimeframeFrame with fractal left=right=k for k in {2,3,5}. Everything else identical. Stouffer over the same 14 cells.
swing_parameter_sensitivity.verdict: FAILS for nested_pullback: the OOS sign flips with the fractal width (+2.67, -0.54, +2.81). The headline is a function of a parameter nobody tuned deliberately, which is the definition of parameter sensitivity. PASSES, weakly, for nested_resumption: positive OOS at all three widths (+1.84, +4.97, +1.95) though IS is negative at k=2 and k=5. nested_aligned swings from z=-4.54 to z=+3.74 IS across k - the incumbent is not even stable enough to be reliably bad.

cost_sensitivity.method: Same strategies re-run at zero cost and at doubled commission plus doubled slippage coefficients (base 1.0 tick, stop extra 2.0, thin 2.0, news 4.0).
cost_sensitivity.verdict: Costs are worth roughly 0.04-0.05R per trade at the baseline model and another 0.04R at double. nested_pullback is negative OOS at every cost level including zero, so its failure is not a cost artefact. nested_resumption stays positive OOS at doubled costs (+0.078R), which is the one robustness test it passes cleanly.

ablation_is_it_the_nesting_or_the_break.identity: nested_resumption is ALGEBRAICALLY IDENTICAL to nested_pullback AND break_of_structure@LTF - same trades, same n=157, same e=+0.1182R, same z in all five periods. It is a conjunction of existing material plus the nesting, not a new primitive, and it should be described that way.
ablation_is_it_the_nesting_or_the_break.verdict: Removing EITHER half destroys the OOS result, and the halves have 4-12x the sample. So the nesting requirement is doing work that a lower-timeframe break of structure on its own does not. That is the single most encouraging number in the study - and it still rests on 157 trades.

independence_correction.method: MGC and MCL are independent contracts; MES/MNQ/NQ are one index complex and were Stouffer-combined into a single unit first. 240/60 only, so no two cells share bars.

nested_pullback.note: the sign REVERSES between IS and OOS in every one of the five symbols; the index complex carried it in sample and the metals/energy carried it out of sample. That is not an effect, that is period-by-symbol noise.

nested_resumption.note: 4 of 5 symbols positive OOS including BOTH independent contracts

deflation.verdict: free_t(1785) = 3.87 t-units are bought by search alone. The best out-of-sample trade-level t-statistic in the whole study is +1.22 (nested_resumption, 157 trades). NOTHING here clears deflation. The largest |t| in the raw rows is +5.03 on THREE trades, which is the sample-size trap the brief warns about.

bias_checks_run.look_ahead_and_repainting: CHECKED, PASSED. TimeframeFrame._build_swing_pointers advances only on confirmed_index <= i, so structure_trend, last/prior_swing_* and swing_leg() cannot repaint. SymbolFrame._build_alignment maps a base bar to the last HTF bar whose end_ts <= this bar's end_ts, so the higher timeframe read is always a CLOSED bar.
bias_checks_run.future_data_leakage: CHECKED, PASSED. Frames are built over full history but run_portfolio(start, end) only permits entries inside the window, and snapshot(i) is backward-only, so OOS warmup uses real prior data without leaking forward.
bias_checks_run.unrealistic_fills: CHECKED. Engine fills entries at the NEXT bar's open, gaps fill at the open, and when a bar contains both stop and target the stop wins.
bias_checks_run.understated_costs: CHECKED, quantified above. Doubling costs moves expectancy by about 0.04R; no conclusion changes sign because of costs.
bias_checks_run.data_mining_bias: CHECKED, FAILED for the headline. free_t = 3.87 and the best OOS t is 1.22.
bias_checks_run.parameter_sensitivity: CHECKED, FAILED for nested_pullback (OOS z flips sign across fractal widths 2/3/5) and for nested_aligned. Weakly passed by nested_resumption.
bias_checks_run.insufficient_sample: CHECKED, FAILED for nested_resumption: 0 of 224 OOS (base, cell) rows reach 20 trades; 157 OOS trades in total for the pure arm.
bias_checks_run.overfitting_is_to_oos: CHECKED. nested_pullback: IS z=+1.87 -> OOS z=-0.54. nested_resumption is the inverse: flat IS, positive OOS - which is not the overfitting signature but is equally a reason to distrust a single split.
bias_checks_run.survivorship: NOT APPLICABLE in the usual sense - single continuous front-month series per symbol, no universe selection. Every generated strategy is reported including the zero-trade and losing ones; no trade floor was used to select the headline arms.
bias_checks_run.clone_collapse: DELIBERATELY OFF. Collapsing identical trade sets would have destroyed the (base+arm) vs (base) pairing. The ablation exploits this: nested_resumption and nested_pullback+break_of_structure produced byte-identical rows, which is how their identity was discovered.

depth.definition: Depth = fraction of the HIGHER timeframe's last confirmed impulse leg that price has retraced, computed from swing_leg() and the swing prices: (leg_high - close)/(leg_high - leg_low) for an up leg. Buckets shallow [0,0.333), medium [0.333,0.618), deep [0.618,1.05). The leg direction is required to match the HTF trend, which is why the three buckets do not sum to nested_pullback's firing rate.
depth.firing_rates: shallow 1.5-3.5%, medium 1.5-4.2%, deep 1.3-6.2% of bars per cell
depth.verdict: No depth band survives. MEDIUM (0.333-0.618) is the only bucket positive vs htf_trend in BOTH IS (z=+2.72) and OOS (z=+2.37) - but its absolute pooled expectancy is negative in both (-0.007R on 199 trades IS, -0.041R on 197 OOS), so it is 'less bad than htf_trend', not an edge; and it flips to z=-2.14 on disjoint slice S1. SHALLOW is significantly NEGATIVE out of sample (z=-3.65 vs htf_trend, z=-4.05 vs no structure). DEEP reverses sign between adjacent disjoint slices (S1 z=+2.72, S2 z=-4.66), which is the signature of noise, not of a band that works.

timeframe_pair.verdict: The tf pair matters, but not in the way the nesting-ratio hypothesis predicts. ALL of nested_pullback's in-sample strength is in 240/60 (IS z=+3.13, S2 z=+6.26, 5 cells) and that is exactly where it dies out of sample (OOS z=-0.45, S3 z=-1.57). 60/15 has the SAME 4:1 nesting ratio and shows nothing anywhere (IS -0.50, OOS -1.25, S1 0.00, S2 +0.75, S3 +0.25). 1440/240 (6:1) is flat throughout (|z| < 1.5 in all five periods). Same ratio, opposite in-sample answer: the ratio is not the driver, the 240/60 result is a frame-specific artefact.

distinctness.nested_pullback vs pullback_to_support: Jaccard 0.06-0.15 across 14 cells; on the overlap only 26-64% agree on direction. Distinct.
distinctness.nested_pullback vs fib_golden_pocket: Jaccard 0.05-0.09; 26-65% direction agreement on the overlap. Distinct.
distinctness.nested_pullback vs structure_trend@LTF: Jaccard 0.23-0.33 but direction agreement 0.00 on EVERY overlapping bar in all 14 cells. nested_pullback is the sign-flip of structure_trend@LTF on the subset of bars where the higher timeframe disagrees. This is the honest description of it.
distinctness.nested_pullback vs structure_trend@HTF (: Jaccard 0.23-0.32, direction agreement 1.00. nested_pullback is a strict SUBSET of structure_trend bound to the higher timeframe, so htf_only is the control it must beat, not 'nothing'.
distinctness.nested_aligned vs mtf_aligned on a TWO-m: Jaccard 1.00 and direction agreement 1.00 in all 5 symbols. Confirms the brief: with two voters mtf_aligned carries no information beyond pairwise agreement. On 240/60 and 60/15 (three-member frames) Jaccard falls to 0.26-0.40.

degeneracy.nested_pullback: 13.4-20.5% of bars - usable, neither degenerate nor a tautology
degeneracy.nested_resumption: 1.6-3.9% - above the 1% floor but thin; expect small trade counts

verdict.statement: NOTHING in this study is live-eligible. The core nesting claim (nested_pullback) is refuted out of sample. nested_resumption is a surviving HYPOTHESIS with a coherent mechanism, an ablation that isolates the nesting, cost robustness and swing-parameter robustness - and a sample far too small to act on. It needs a dedicated run at a lower trade floor across more symbols and more exits before anyone should look at it again.
verdict.recommendation_for_the_library: Do NOT lift the mtf_not_conflicted veto on the strength of nested_pullback. DO stop treating nested_aligned/mtf_aligned as evidence: on any two-member frame it is bar-for-bar identical to pairwise agreement, it is worse than no structure condition at all (z=-4.14 IS, -3.73 independence-corrected), and its sign flips with the swing fractal width.
